name: Greek yoghurt
summary: Greek yoghurt is thick, tangy yoghurt that has been strained. This page lists what people say it does and what a writer in ancient Rome believed about soured milk; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose.
inIt: The UK food table (CoFID) measures plain Greek-style yoghurt at 133 kcal, 5.7 g of protein, 10.2 g of fat (6.8 g of it saturated), 4.5 g of sugars, 126 mg of calcium and 39 µg of iodine per 100 g, with no fibre. That entry is a full-fat one. The table does not measure the live bacteria or the peptides that fermenting makes.

Yoghurt's lactose is digested more efficiently than the lactose in other dairy foods, because the bacteria in yoghurt help to digest it. A review of the studies says the bacterial lactase survives the stomach's acid, protected inside the bacterial cells, and is active in the small intestine, enough to prevent symptoms in lactose-intolerant people.

lore.who: Ancient Rome (Pliny the Elder, about 77 AD)
lore.belief: Pliny described oxygala, a soured milk made by adding sour milk to the fresh milk that is to curdle, and said that this preparation is extremely wholesome to the stomach.
lore.note: Pliny does not describe straining the curd, so this is not evidence about Greek-style yoghurt itself, only about soured, curdled milk.

sources.title: Pliny the Elder, Natural History 28.36 (oxygala: one remedy), Bostock and Riley translation, 1855
sources.author: Pliny the Elder

tableFoods.label: 1 small pot of plain Greek-style yoghurt (about 150 g)

processing: Flavour changes the sugar: in the UK food table, plain Greek-style yoghurt has 4.5 g of sugars per 100 g and the fruit version 10.5 g.

Greek-style is not the same as other plain yoghurt: the table lists plain whole-milk yoghurt at 7.8 g of sugars and 200 mg of calcium per 100 g, against 4.5 g and 126 mg in plain Greek-style, with the same 5.7 g of protein.

whoShouldBeCareful.note: Yoghurt is still made from milk. In a challenge study of 34 children with IgE-mediated cow's milk allergy, 11 of the 31 who had reacted to milk with whole-body symptoms also reacted to yoghurt. If you or your child have a milk allergy, talk to your doctor or allergist before trying it.

unknowns: Whether Greek-style yoghurt differs from other yoghurt in any health outcome: no human study of Greek yoghurt on its own was found for this page, and the reviews cited here cover yoghurt in general.

Whether eating yoghurt itself lowers the risk of death or heart disease: in the pooled cohort studies, high intake went with a lower risk of dying (relative risk 0.93, 95% interval 0.89 to 0.98) and of cardiovascular death (0.89, 0.81 to 0.98), but studies that only watch people cannot show cause.
Whether yoghurt helps with weight: a review of ten cohort studies found the link to overweight and obesity not fully consistent or always statistically significant.
